long_biography.plain_text:
For banker Hüsnü Özyeğin, expanding girls' education meant first providing somewhere for them to live. After learning how few girls in an outlying Turkish province continued beyond primary school, his foundation built dormitories near urban high schools. The accommodation enabled girls from poorer areas to continue their education.

He also established Özyeğin University, where his group funded scholarships and courses included engineering, hotel management and civil aviation. His own studies abroad had required paid work alongside scholarships, including serving food and running a campus cafeteria. He took a personal interest in student life, visiting the campus and accompanying graduates on overseas trips.
